$comment: Which vector families each §8 conformance level requires. This file is SCOPE, never ORACLE: it names files and cites the sentence that puts them at a level, and contains no expected value from any case. Expected values live in vectors/ and are read from there at run time. Keeping the mapping here rather than in code is deliberate — it is the one part of the runner that is a reading of §8 rather than a fact about the vectors, so it should be readable and arguable without opening a .mjs file.

canonicalization.basis: §0 Conventions (RFC 8785 JCS). Every identifier, hash and signing preimage in the protocol is defined over the canonical form, so a node that cannot canonicalize cannot reach any level.

derivation.basis: §1.1–§1.2. A persona_id IS the public key; the whole verification model rests on the derivation being the one §1.1 specifies.

hashing.basis: §3.2. L0 (vault): the commitment_hash is what fan-out shares (M-3).

envelope-id.basis: §2. §8 puts the envelope in the Node level via M-19; the id preimage is the other half of §2 and is meaningless without it.

envelope-bounds.basis: M-19, named explicitly in the Node level: "a node MUST NOT canonicalize an envelope exceeding the §2 bounds".

transitions-invalid.basis: M-14, named in the Node level: "Assertions violating the transition table are invalid and MUST be discarded".

visibility.basis: §5.3, M-4. Reached at the Node level through the range M-1..M-16. §8 named this family as v0 suite scope for months while it did not exist; it does now, and the entry that used to sit in this level's `unreachable` list has moved here.

node-surface-actions.basis: M-20, named in the Node level and again in the Client level. §8: "M-21 on open_loops by actions.json".

node-surface-act-tool.basis: M-20, named in the Node level: "MUST NOT bind an advertised act to a tool call that produces no assertion". The Client half of M-20 — "MUST NOT invent a tool binding for an act the node reports as unbound" — is the same vocabulary read from the other side.

node-surface-brief-slots.basis: M-21. §8 names M-21 in the Client level ONLY — the Node level lists M-1..M-16, M-19, M-20 — yet §8 also says "the node halves of both are covered by the node-surface vectors: ... on brief by brief-slots.json", and every case in the file judges what a NODE may emit. See findings/1 in README.md. Required for Client, advisory for Node.

node-surface-verification-levels.basis: M-12. Reached at the Node level through the range M-1..M-16, and named again at the Client level. See findings/2 in README.md.

addressing-inbox.basis: §6.7, M-17. M-17 is outside the Node range (M-1..M-16, M-19, M-20) and arrives only through the Federating node's "+ §6".

recovery.basis: §6.6, named explicitly in the Federating node level: "recovery responder".

levels.title: Node
levels.quote: Node (minimum): L0–L1 + §7 six tools + M-1..M-16, M-19, M-20.
unreachable: M-1, M-3, M-5, M-6, M-7, M-10, M-13, M-15, M-16 have no vector family. They are Node MUSTs that no case in vectors/ exercises; passing this level says nothing about them. M-9 left this list when transitions/ gained the collective-edge cases, and M-4 when visibility/ was written — the list is maintained by subtraction, so an entry that stays is one nobody has been able to remove rather than one nobody has looked at.
§7's six tools are exercised only through act, confirm-binding and brief/open_loops shapes. There is no vector that enumerates the six or checks that a node offers all of them.
The 256-level canonicalizer refusal depth (envelope/bounds.json, canonicalizer_refusal) is stated "rather than given a case" and is not checked.

M-8 is covered only in the half a vector can reach: `expected_unverifiable` pins that a node computes the flag auto-escalation is gated on. Whether it then declines to escalate is a local decision this runner cannot observe.

levels.title: Federating node
levels.quote: Federating node: + §6 (one transport, recon, recovery responder).
unreachable: "one transport" — no vector family exercises a transport. §6.1–§6.2 wire behaviour is entirely outside the suite.
"recon" (§6.4 reconciliation) — no vector family. The suite checks the recovery responder (§6.6) and addressing (§6.7) only.

The out-of-band serialization is an INTERPRETATION, not normative (vectors/README.md, gap 9): §6.7 fixes no serialization for the URL/QR form. Passing addressing-oob shows agreement with the suite's choice, not with the spec.

levels.title: Hub
unreachable: §6.3 blind-courier requirements — no vector family exists.

M-11 (no network-level reputation) — §8's suite scope names "M-11 negative tests" as v0 scope, and no such family exists in vectors/. A negative of this shape is also the hardest kind to write as a vector: it pins the absence of a computation, and a request/response probe cannot see a statistic a hub keeps and does not serve.

levels.title: Client
levels.quote: Client: §7 consumer + M-12, M-20 and M-21 display rules.
unreachable: The client halves of M-12 and M-21 — "MUST NOT render an attested display name above its evidence level", "a client MUST author the wording of every affordance it renders" — are not reachable by vectors. §8: "A vector pins what a node emits. It cannot inspect what a client paints." They are judged by a rendered-fact-set harness (@servanda/client-conformance), not by this runner.

The four families above pin the NODE halves. Passing them shows the implementation agrees about what may cross the node surface; it says nothing about what it draws. This is why the Client level can reach `partial` here and never `pass`.
